answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a web of costly peer endorsements: a newcomer only gains spending rights after established agents vouch for it, and each voucher risks its own reputation score if the newcomer misbehaves. A fake identity cannot forge trust out of thin air - it must earn links from real participants, and those links are scarce, like opal veins in rock. Graph analysis then spots the saffron-stained clusters of mutually endorsing fakes, because genuine agents connect broadly while sybils only connect to each other.
